# Build cache notes

The CI job restores its dependency cache from a key made of the runner image and the branch name.
When the lockfile changes the key stays the same, so the restored store no longer matches it and
the install step refuses it. Rebuilding by hand fixes one run, then the next lockfile change breaks it again.

## Ideas

- hash the lockfile into the key;
- keep a restore key without the hash, so most packages still come from the cache;
- share one store between branches that have the same lockfile.

content.text:
The CI job builds its dependency cache key from the runner image and the branch name only. When the lockfile changes, the key stays the same, so CI restores a store that no longer matches the lockfile, and the install step rejects it. Rebuilding the cache by hand fixes one run, but the next lockfile change breaks it again.

The fix is to include a hash of the lockfile in the cache key, so any lockfile change produces a new key. The notes also suggest a fallback restore key without the hash, so most packages still come from the cache. They suggest sharing one store between branches with the same lockfile too. I appended the line "Reviewed: the lockfile hash goes into the cache key." to `notes.md` and changed no other file. The file already ended with a newline, so a blank line now sits before the new line.
